# Vehicle type {#sec-dd-vehicle-type}


::: {.cell}

:::


## Overview

These columns say what kind of vehicle each row is. The sources classify
vehicles in different ways, none of which matches the categories most analyses
want, so the pipeline harmonises them. @sec-vehicle-types explains the
classifications and how they relate.

- **`body_type`** is the DfT body type: Cars, Light goods vehicles,
  Motorcycles, Buses and coaches, Heavy goods vehicles or Other vehicles. It is
  the usual way to select, for example, cars only. `body_type_src` records
  whether it came from the DfT model, the DVLA type approval, the generic model
  or the MOT test class (methodology,
  [section 4.6](../../reports/methodology.md#body-type)).
- **`test_class`** is the MOT test class (1 to 7) and **`type_approval`** the
  European type approval category (M1, N1, L3 and so on). Both take the
  recorded value where there is one (`test_class_ANON` and the DVLA type
  approval), and otherwise the most common value among similar vehicles that
  share the other one, first of the same make, model, birth year, fuel and
  engine size, then of the same make, model, birth year and fuel. A borrowed
  value that contradicts the other classifications, the wheel plan or the
  engine size is not used. Each has a `_src` column saying which (methodology,
  [section 5.6](../../reports/methodology.md#other-attributes)).
- **The supplied columns** (`_DVLA`, `_ANON`) are the values as received,
  including the DVLA flag for automated vehicles, which the pipeline does not
  use.

The vehicle's colour, wheel plan and weight are described in @sec-dd-colour,
@sec-dd-wheelplan and @sec-dd-weight.

## Coverage

`body_type` is present for 97% of vehicles and
changes little with age (@fig-dd-vehicle-type). The vehicles without one are
those whose model could not be matched and which have no type approval or test
class to fall back on.

The other harmonised columns depend on what their sources hold:

- **`type_approval`** is rare for vehicles first used before 2000
  (26%), because the DVLA rarely
  records a type approval category for them, and the backfill can only copy
  values that similar vehicles have. From the mid-2000s it is present for more
  than 90%.
- **`test_class`** comes from the anonymised MOT data, so it is present only
  for vehicles that have been tested, or are like vehicles that have. Coverage
  falls for vehicles first used since 2023, which are too new for their first
  MOT test: 78% for 2025.

`typeApproval_DVLA` shares the pattern of every VES field, being present only
where a VES record was found (@sec-dd-dvla-status). `automatedVehicle_DVLA`
is present only for some vehicles first used since 2021
(25% of those first used in 2025).

## Values

How the values of each column change over time, by year of first use, from 1990. Numeric columns and
dates show the minimum, lower quartile (Q1), median, upper quartile (Q3) and
maximum; other columns show the share of vehicles with each value, with the
less common values grouped as *All other values* and missing values as
*Blank*.


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

### `body_type`

DfT body type: Cars, Light goods vehicles, Motorcycles, Buses and coaches, Heavy goods vehicles or Other vehicles (see body_type_src).


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Share of vehicles by value of body_type, by year of first use.](vehicle-type_files/figure-html/fig-dd-v-body-type-1.png){#fig-dd-v-body-type fig-align='center' width=1050}
:::
:::


### `body_type_src`

Source of body_type: model (the DfT model string's body type), type_approval (DVLA type approval, where the generic model has that body type), genmodel (the generic model's most common body type) or test_class.


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Share of vehicles by value of body_type_src, by year of first use.](vehicle-type_files/figure-html/fig-dd-v-body-type-src-1.png){#fig-dd-v-body-type-src fig-align='center' width=1050}
:::
:::


### `test_class`

MOT test class: test_class_ANON, else the most common class of similar vehicles with the same recorded type approval (variant, then model_year_fuel), else of similar vehicles born at least backfill.test_class_min_age years before the last year, so that minibuses (first tested at one year) do not outnumber vans and cars (three); a borrowed class that contradicts the type approval, wheel plan or engine size is not used (test_class_src conflict). Imputed for vehicles never tested and for most vehicles in Northern Ireland (the anonymised class is missing for NI tests); the backfill does not use weight, so a van near the class 4 / 7 boundary can take the wrong class.


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Share of vehicles by value of test_class, by year of first use.](vehicle-type_files/figure-html/fig-dd-v-test-class-1.png){#fig-dd-v-test-class fig-align='center' width=1050}
:::
:::


### `test_class_src`

Source of the matching harmonised column: dvsa or dvla (recorded), variant (same make/model/birth year/fuel/engine size) or model_year_fuel (same make/model/birth year/fuel).


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
